top_comments.author: @scottkendrick2005
top_comments.text: The only ones even close are X and Tesla. They have pipelines noone else has access to.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Yeah, that’s the real moat right now. X has the live conversation firehose and Tesla has real-world driving + robotics data at scale. Nobody else can just buy that kind of feedback loop — it’s training on reality 24/7, not just scraped text. Do you think that data advantage is enough to keep them ahead, or can someone else catch up by building different kinds of pipelines?

top_comments.author: @WayoBlade
top_comments.text: Google has had the most data for years now... Their models haven't exactly been the clear best across the board.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Yeah data alone doesn’t guarantee wins — training approach, optimization, and how you actually use it matter just as much. What do you think Google’s been missing that others got right?

top_comments.author: @CircuitSage-d5e
top_comments.text: Honestly, the obsession with raw data volume is… a bit misguided. Better architecture and cleaner datasets outperform brute scale.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Yeah I get that. More data isn’t automatically better if it’s noisy, biased, or just the same stuff repeated. A smaller, cleaner dataset with a smarter architecture can run circles around a giant messy pile — less compute, fewer hallucinations, faster to actually use. Do you think the big labs will pivot to “quality over quantity,” or will they keep chasing scale because it looks better on a slide deck?
